evals.name: review-whitespace-slot-fallback
evals.prompt: Can you review this skip link component? It passed every test but an accessibility audit flagged an empty link on a couple of pages. ```html Skip to content ``` The layout calls it like this: ```html ```
evals.expected_output: Triggers. Identifies that the newline inside is a text node assigned to the default slot, so the fallback never renders and the output is , an empty link. Recommends an @label prop with a default instead of a default-slot fallback, and a fixture test rendering the newline case. Also notes the HTML comment ships to every page and that skip-link sets no display on its tag.

evals.name: review-container-selector-leak
evals.expected_output: Triggers. Explains that both selectors have equal specificity and WebC bundle order decides the winner, so the container rule leaks into the slotted component. Fix: wrap the container rule in :where() (rich-text :where(ul, ol)) or anchor it with a child combinator, and optionally make the component rule slightly more specific. Suggests a test that flags bare descendant selectors in slot-taking components.

evals.name: boolean-prop-false-is-truthy
evals.prompt: In my WebC segmented control, `<segmented-control @icon-only="false">` still hides the labels. The template has `<fieldset :data-icon-only="iconOnly ? '' : undefined">`. Why?
evals.expected_output: Triggers. Explains that @icon-only="false" passes the string "false", which is truthy; only :@icon-only="false" passes a boolean. Recommends one truthiness expression for every boolean prop (x === true || x === '' || x === 'true'), documented once, and a table-driven fixture test.

evals.name: style-undefined-crash
evals.prompt: Eleventy build fails with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toString')" after I added this to card.webc: `<div :style="accent ? `--accent: ${accent}` : undefined">`. Other attributes with undefined work fine.
evals.expected_output: Triggers. Explains that WebC merges style and class with .toString(), so a dynamic style or class must never evaluate to undefined; return an empty string instead. Notes every other attribute may be undefined safely, which is why only this one fails.

evals.name: author-component-oblique
evals.prompt: Build me a notice banner component for our Eleventy site. It has a title, body content, an optional dismiss button, and a variant (info, warning, error). We use .webc files for everything.
evals.expected_output: Triggers without the word WebC. Puts title and body in slots and variant/dismiss in props, sets display on the host tag (kept because the file has a <style>), normalizes the dismissible boolean with one truthiness expression, makes the dismiss label overridable by a prop, wraps the client script in a block and registers a guarded custom element, and suggests fixture tests for the whitespace and "false" cases.

evals.name: negative-eleventy-config
evals.prompt: How do I set up passthrough copy for my images folder in eleventy.config.js and change the output directory to dist?
evals.expected_output: Does NOT trigger. This is Eleventy configuration with no WebC component involved.

evals.name: negative-lit-component-review
evals.prompt: Review my Lit web component: a <user-card> with a reactive `name` property, shadow DOM styles, and a slot for the avatar. Is the slot fallback a good idea?
evals.expected_output: Does NOT trigger. A Lit custom element with shadow DOM: slot assignment happens in the browser, not in the WebC compiler, so WebC rules do not apply. The design-system skill or a direct answer fits better.

evals.name: negative-nunjucks-macro
evals.prompt: My Nunjucks macro for a card component renders an empty heading when I forget the title argument. How do I give it a default?
evals.expected_output: Does NOT trigger. A Nunjucks macro, not a WebC component; answer with Nunjucks default arguments.
